attempts.summary: Created a LUKS-encrypted, file-backed volume (/var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img) on node1, formatted ext4, and mounted it at /srv/secure. Auto-unlock at boot uses a root-only keyfile (/etc/luks-keys/secure.key, mode 400) referenced from /etc/crypttab, and /etc/fstab mounts /dev/mapper/secure at /srv/secure. Verified the systemd-generated units (systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service, srv-secure.mount) are wired into local-fs.target. Rebooted node1 via the mandatory restart protocol; boot_id changed from 2f708738-... to 4251f85b-..., and post-reboot the volume was unlocked and mounted automatically with the pre-restart test file intact — no manual unlock step was needed.
